chapter.chapter: Chapter 4 — The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition

excerpts:
[CBSE Class XII Economics, sample question paper, 2022-23]
11. Suppose in a hypothetical economy there are only two Firms A and B, Firm A sold goods
for ₹ 2,000 to Firm B and purchased goods for ₹ 1,000. Firm B exported goods for ₹ 2,500 3
and had domestic sales of ₹ 1,500. Calculate Net Domestic Product at market price, if
consumption of fixed capital is ₹ 200.

[CBSE Class XII Economics, marking scheme, 2025-26]
11. Gross Value Added of Firm B = (i) – (iv) ½
= 1,000 – 250 = ₹ 750 crore ½
Gross Value Added of Firm A = Gross Value Added of Firm B = ₹ 750 crore
Domestic Sales of Firm A = Gross Value Added of Firm A – (iii) – (v) + (ii) 1
= 750 – 200 – 150 + 300 ½
= ₹ 700 crore ½

[CBSE Class XII Economics, marking scheme, 2026-27]
10. (C) 1, infinity 1
11 A Value-Added Method:
Gross Domestic Product at Market Price = (ii) - (viii) ½
= 1,900 – 330 ½
= ₹ 1,570 crore ½
Expenditure Method:
Gross Domestic Product at Market Price = (i) + (iii) + (iv) + (vii) ½
= 500 + 400 + 600 + 70 ½
= ₹ 1,570 crore ½
OR
11 B (I) Two factors of production and their respective remunerations earned are:
• Land - Rent ½ + ½
• Capital - Interest ½ + ½
(II) The remuneration earned by the Land can be defined as:
Rent: Income earned by the owner of the land (natural resources). 1

[CBSE Class XII Economics, marking scheme, 2024-25]

items.stem: Based on the passage, what does it mean for a firm to be a 'price taker'?
What is the main characteristic of a firm in a perfectly competitive market?
If a firm in a perfectly competitive market sells its product at a price higher than the market price, what will happen?
Why is the total revenue curve for a price-taking firm a straight line?
In a perfectly competitive market, what does the price line represent for a firm?
If a firm in a perfectly competitive market sells 10 units of a product at ₹ 50 each, what is its total revenue?
A firm in a perfectly competitive market faces a market price of ₹ 50. Its total cost function is TC = 100 + 10q, where q is the quantity produced. What is the profit-maximising level of output?
A firm sells its product at a price of ₹ 50. The total variable cost for producing 100 units is ₹ 3,000, and the total fixed cost is ₹ 2,000. What is the firm's total profit?
A firm is producing where the market price is equal to the short run average variable cost. What is the firm's decision regarding production?
What is the firm's profit at the output level q in the short run?
In the long run, a firm will exit the market if the market price is below its long run average cost. Why is this the case?
Which of the following is true about a firm's short run supply curve?
What happens to a firm's supply curve when there is a technological progress?
A firm sells its product at a price of ₹ 60. It has total fixed costs of ₹ 1,000 and total variable costs of ₹ 4,000. What is the firm's profit if it produces 100 units?
According to the passage, what is the definition of price elasticity of supply?
If the market price is less than the minimum long run average cost, what will the firm do in the long run?
What is the effect of an increase in input prices on a firm's supply curve?
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between market price and marginal revenue for a price-taking firm?
Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between market price and average revenue for a price-taking firm?
A firm is producing 100 units of output and selling each unit at a market price of Rs 10. What is the total revenue of the firm?

A firm sells its product at a market price of Rs 10. It sells 50 units and earns a total revenue of Rs 500. If the price increases to Rs 15 and the firm sells 100 units, what is the price elasticity of supply?

The price elasticity of supply of a good is calculated as the percentage change in quantity supplied divided by the percentage change in price. According to the passage, what is the price elasticity of supply when the supply curve is a straight line passing through the origin?
If a profit-maximising firm produces a positive level of output in a competitive market, what must be true about the market price and marginal cost?
A firm's supply curve is upward sloping. If the price of an input used in production increases, what will happen to the firm's supply curve?

In a perfectly competitive market, a firm's short-run supply curve is defined as the rising part of the short-run marginal cost curve from and above the minimum average variable cost. If a firm's short-run marginal cost is Rs 50 at the minimum average variable cost, what is the minimum price the firm would accept to continue production?
According to the passage, what is the condition for a firm to produce a positive output in the short run?
If the market price is below the minimum long run average cost (LRAC), what will a profit-maximising firm do in the long run?
A firm operating in a perfectly competitive market has a minimum AVC of ₹ 50 and a minimum LRAC of ₹ 80. If the market price is ₹ 60, what will the firm do in the short run and long run?
According to the passage, when a firm produces zero output, what is its profit?
What is the main assumption about a firm's behaviour in a perfectly competitive market?
What is the relationship between marginal revenue and market price for a firm in perfect competition?
A firm in a perfectly competitive market sells its product at a market price of ₹ 10 per unit. If it sells 100 units, what is its total revenue?
What is the primary objective of a firm in the theory of the firm under perfect competition?
What is the relationship between marginal revenue and market price for a perfectly competitive firm?
If the market price is less than the minimum average variable cost, what will a profit-maximising firm choose to do in the short run?
In the short run, a firm in a perfectly competitive market will stop production if the market price falls below its average variable cost. Why is this the case?
